cards.front: UFH in ACS is weight-based because its dose-response is unpredictable. The max bolus cap of [___] units prevents excessive dosing in obese patients.
cards.context:
UFH in ACS: 60 units/kg bolus (max 5000 U) followed by 12 units/kg/hr infusion (max 1000 U/hr), titrated to APTT 1.5-2.5× control.

UFH binds antithrombin to inhibit factors IIa and Xa. Its anti-IIa activity makes it the heparin of choice when reversal might be needed (protamine fully reverses UFH but only ~60% of LMWH).

cards.front: In septic shock, target MAP is ≥[___] mmHg with lactate >2 mmol/L despite adequate fluids.
cards.context: Septic shock is a subset of sepsis with particularly high mortality.

cards.front: A patient develops acute dyspnoea, wheezing, urticaria, and hypotension during an infusion. Give adrenaline 0.5 mg [___].
cards.context: The clinical scenario of acute dyspnoea, wheezing, urticaria, and hypotension during an infusion is classic anaphylaxis.

cards.front: First-line vasopressor in septic shock: noradrenaline. If inadequate response, add vasopressin (works via [___] receptors).
cards.context:
Catecholamine alpha-1 receptors become progressively desensitised after prolonged high-dose stimulation, so escalating a single agent eventually plateaus on MAP.

Adding a non-catecholamine that acts through V1 receptors (vasopressin) restores tone via a parallel pathway, and lets the noradrenaline dose come down.

cards.front: Normal magnesium (Mg²⁺) range is [___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
Mg²⁺ 0.7-1.0 mmol/L. The 'forgotten cation' — Mg deficiency makes hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia refractory to replacement, because Mg is needed for tubular reabsorption of K and parathyroid hormone secretion.

Hypomagnesaemia: alcohol use, diuretics, PPI long-term, GI losses (diarrhoea, ileostomy), refeeding syndrome. Causes torsades, tremor, weakness.

cards.front: Delta ratio: (AG − 12) / (24 − HCO₃). A ratio '<'1 suggests concurrent [___]; '>'2 suggests concurrent metabolic alkalosis.
cards.context:
Delta ratio = (AG − 12) / (24 − HCO₃). Detects second metabolic disorders hidden by HAGMA.

A pure HAGMA has 1:1 relationship between AG rise and HCO₃ fall. Ratio <1 = concurrent NAGMA; 1-2 = pure HAGMA; >2 = concurrent metabolic alkalosis.

cards.front: First-line treatment in anaphylaxis is IM adrenaline using the [___] concentration.
cards.context:
IM adrenaline 1:1000 (1 mg/mL) is the only intervention that addresses *all* features of anaphylaxis simultaneously: α-1 vasoconstriction reverses hypotension and mucosal oedema.

The IM anterolateral thigh route gives faster, more reliable absorption than deltoid even in shock.

cards.front: CPP = MAP − ICP. Target CPP is [___] mmHg. ICP threshold for starting tiered therapy is 22 mmHg.
cards.context:
CPP is the driving pressure for cerebral blood flow. The formula is simple but the targets are critical — CPP below 50 causes ischaemia, above 70 increases ARDS risk from vasopressor use.

ICP above 22 mmHg sustained triggers escalation to tiered therapy.

cards.front: In acute haemorrhage, initial Hb may be normal because the patient loses [___] proportionally, keeping the concentration ratio unchanged.
cards.context:
In acute haemorrhage, the patient loses whole blood (cells and plasma in proportion), so Hb concentration stays normal initially. Hb only drops once haemodilution occurs from fluid shifts or IV fluids (6-24 hours).

Always treat physiology, not the number.

cards.front: Septic shock (Sepsis-3): vasopressors needed for MAP ≥65 AND lactate >[___] despite adequate fluids.
cards.context:
Sepsis-3 (2016) split sepsis (suspected infection + organ dysfunction) from septic shock (sepsis + circulatory failure requiring vasopressor + cellular dysoxia).

Mortality in septic shock is >40% — substantially higher than sepsis without shock. Rapid escalation (Hour-1 bundle) is the response: cultures, antibiotics, fluids 30 mL/kg, vasopressors to MAP ≥65, ICU referral.

cards.front: The first bedside test for any reproductive-age woman with abdominal pain is [___].
cards.context: For any woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain, bedside bHCG is the single most important first test to rule out ectopic pregnancy.

cards.front: Propofol for refractory status epilepticus: 1-2 mg/kg bolus then [___] mg/kg/hr infusion.
cards.context:
Refractory status (failure of two anti-seizure agents) requires general anaesthesia to break the seizure — without it, ongoing electrical activity causes irreversible excitotoxic neuronal injury within hours.

Patient needs intubation (no longer protecting airway), continuous EEG, ICU admission. Watch for propofol infusion syndrome at high doses or prolonged use; consider switching to midazolam or thiopentone if running >48 h.

cards.front: Mast cell tryptase timing: sample immediately, at 1-2 hours (peak), and >24 hours (baseline). It is often falsely normal in [___]-triggered anaphylaxis.
cards.context:
The timing of tryptase samples is a common exam question.

Food-triggered anaphylaxis commonly has normal tryptase, so clinical diagnosis takes precedence.

cards.front: Digoxin Fab fragments are indicated for life-threatening arrhythmias or potassium >[___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
Digoxin toxicity kills via arrhythmia (VT, VF, CHB, junctional tachycardia) and hyperkalaemia from inhibited Na/K-ATPase shifting K out of cells — both findings drive Fab indication.

Fab (Digibind/DigiFab) binds digoxin as inert complexes cleared renally — expensive and limited stock, call pharmacy early.

cards.front: Monitoring frequency for IV maintenance fluids: check U&E at least every 24 hours; more often if electrolytes are [___].
cards.context:
Guidelines (NICE CG174 / RCH) advise checking U&E at least daily while a patient is on IV maintenance fluids — and more often (e.g. 4–6 hourly) if electrolytes are already abnormal or the patient is unstable.

Daily monitoring catches insidious hyponatraemia early.

cards.front: Vasopressin in septic shock is given at a fixed dose of 0.03 units/min and is not [___].
cards.context:
Vasopressin is added when noradrenaline alone fails to reach MAP target (typically once nor exceeds 0.25-0.5 mcg/kg/min).

It is NOT titrated to effect because higher doses cause splanchnic, coronary, and digital ischaemia without proportional MAP gain — a fixed sub-pressor dose is the safe sweet spot.

cards.front: Parkland formula: 4 mL x weight (kg) x %TBSA; timing is calculated from time of [___], not presentation.
cards.context:
Parkland is calculated from time of INJURY, not time of presentation — late presenters need a faster initial fluid rate to deliver the first half within 8 hours of the burn (when capillary leak is greatest).

A patient who presents 4 hours post-burn still needs half the 24-hour total in the next 4 hours. Conversely, fluid started in the field counts toward the total — communicate with retrieval/ambulance about volumes given.

cards.front: Delta ratio 0.8-2.0 indicates [___] HAGMA; <0.8 = mixed HAGMA + NAGMA; >2.0 = HAGMA + metabolic alkalosis.
cards.context:
In a clean HAGMA, every unmeasured anion consumes a bicarbonate — rise in AG and fall in HCO₃ should be ~1:1. Delta ratio formalises that; value 0.8-2.0 says nothing else is going on.

Outside that window a second process is hiding. <0.8 = HCO₃ fell further than AG rose, so a normal-AG acidosis is co-existing (DKA + diarrhoea.

cards.front: Chronic respiratory acidosis compensation: HCO₃ rises [___] mmol/L per 10 mmHg pCO₂ increase above 40.
cards.context:
Chronic respiratory acidosis (e.g. COPD with sustained CO₂ retention) develops renal compensation over 3-5 days: HCO₃⁻ rises ~3.5 mmol/L for each 10 mmHg pCO₂ above 40.

Acute respiratory acidosis raises HCO₃⁻ only ~1 mmol/L per 10 mmHg. If HCO₃⁻ is HIGHER than expected for the pCO₂ rise, suspect superimposed metabolic alkalosis (e.g. diuretic use).

If LOWER, suspect a coexisting metabolic acidosis.

cards.front: Pulmonary fibrosis impairs gas exchange by increasing membrane [___].
cards.context: In pulmonary fibrosis, collagen deposition thickens the interstitium between alveolar epithelium and capillary endothelium — gas must diffuse further, reducing transfer rate per Fick's law.

cards.front: VBG-to-ABG conversion: arterial pH is approximately [___] higher than venous, and arterial pCO₂ is 3–8 mmHg lower.
cards.context:
The VBG-to-ABG difference comes from venous CO₂ accumulation in tissues. pH is consistently ~0.03 higher arterially; pCO₂ is 3-8 mmHg lower arterially.

VBG is reliable for pH, pCO₂, HCO₃⁻, and lactate trending in most ICU contexts; ABG remains needed when accurate PaO₂ is required (oxygenation assessment.

cards.front: Parkland formula timing is calculated from time of injury, not presentation. The first half is given over [___] hours.
cards.context:
Parkland formula: 4 mL x body weight (kg) x %TBSA burned. Give the first half over the first 8 hours from the TIME OF INJURY (not time of presentation).

Give the second half over the next 16 hours. This is a common exam mistake — always calculate from time of burn, not arrival to hospital.

cards.front: Severe chest pain with diaphoresis is ATS Category [___] with a maximum wait of 10 minutes.
cards.context:
Severe chest pain with diaphoresis is treated as suspected ACS until proven otherwise — Category 2 (imminently life-threatening) with a 10-minute target.

Category 2 also covers active severe pain unresponsive to ED analgesia, severe head injury, severe trauma, and altered consciousness from any cause.

cards.front: Per CRASH-2, trauma TXA dosing is [___] IV bolus over 10 min, then the same dose given as an infusion over 8 hours. Beyond 3 hours from injury, the mortality benefit is lost — and may even be harmful.
cards.context:
CRASH-2 (Lancet 2010, n=20,211): TXA cuts all-cause mortality by 1.5% absolute (NNT ~67) when given within 3 hours of injury.

Mechanism: blocks plasminogen activation, preventing fibrinolysis without promoting new clot formation.

Protocol: same dose for bolus (over 10 min) and 8-hour infusion — the symmetry makes it easy to recall under stress.

cards.front: Post-arrest ABG targets? SpO₂: 94–98% (avoid hyperoxia). PaCO₂: 35–45 mmHg (normocapnia). Acidosis: treat the cause, not pH (bicarb only if pH < [___]).
cards.context:
Post-ROSC hyperoxia worsens neurological outcomes via free radical injury. Hypocapnia reduces cerebral perfusion; hypercapnia increases ICP.

Bicarbonate generates CO₂ — rarely indicated unless pH below 7.1.

cards.front: Lactate clearance = ([___] − current) ÷ baseline × 100. An adequate response is ≥10–20% clearance within 2–4 hours.
cards.context:
Lactate clearance is the rate of fall from the initial value, not the absolute number. Started at 8, now 6 = 25% cleared (responding, even though 6 is still grossly abnormal).

Trajectory guides escalation. Failure to clear in the first few hours of fluids + antibiotics signals inadequate source control — go looking for an undrained collection, missed bowel ischaemia, or dead limb.

cards.front: The GCS threshold for intubation is [___] or below.
cards.context:
At GCS ≤8 the gag and cough reflexes plus tongue tone become unreliable, so the airway is no longer self-protected and aspiration risk rises sharply.

Intubate before transfer or imaging rather than waiting for the patient to aspirate or obstruct.

cards.front: Normal urea range is [___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
Urea 3.0-8.0 mmol/L. Generated by hepatic urea cycle from amino acid catabolism, freely filtered then partially reabsorbed (especially when renal flow is low — pre-renal AKI).

Markedly raised urea + normal creatinine in a patient with GI bleeding is digested blood absorbed as protein load. Urea also rises with steroid-driven catabolism, GI bleeding, and high-protein feeds.

cards.front: In massive transfusion, target pH above [___] to avoid coagulopathy.
cards.context:
The trauma triad of death (hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy) is a lethal combination that is self-perpetuating. Each element worsens the others.

All MTP targets are designed to break this cycle.

cards.front: First-line diuretic in acute pulmonary oedema is IV [___] (loop diuretic to reduce preload).
cards.context: The classic bundle for acute pulmonary oedema. Modern practice leans on nitrates, non-invasive ventilation (CPAP) and diuresis; routine morphine is now discouraged as it is linked to worse outcomes.

cards.front: First-line treatment for eclamptic seizures is magnesium sulphate, given as a [___] slow IV bolus.
cards.context: Eclamptic seizures have specific management — magnesium sulphate is first-line, NOT benzodiazepines.

cards.front: P/F ratio = PaO₂ ÷ FiO₂. A P/F of 150 classifies as [___] ARDS by Berlin criteria.
cards.context:
Berlin ARDS criteria stratify severity by P/F ratio (PaO₂ ÷ FiO₂ as decimal): mild 200-300 (e.g. PaO₂ 60 on FiO₂ 0.3), moderate 100-200, severe ≤100. Stratification is calculated on PEEP ≥5 cmH₂O — without that floor.

Severity drives intervention: mild ARDS responds to NIV/HFNO + lung-protective ventilation; moderate adds proning consideration if persistent (PROSEVA threshold P/F <150); severe t.

P/F replaces the A-a gradient as the standard oxygenation index in ventilated patients because A-a widens artificially with FiO₂.

cards.front: Ottawa Ankle Rules: X-ray if tenderness at posterior lateral or medial malleolus (distal 6 cm), base of [___] metatarsal, navicular bone, or unable to weight-bear 4 steps.
cards.context: The Ottawa rules check four bony areas plus weight-bearing ability. The midfoot component (base of 5th MT and navicular) is often forgotten but catches important fractures that can be missed clinically.
